subject: general
question: When a ray of light passes through the optical centre of a spherical lens, it _______.

options.text: Gets deviated away from the normal

solution:
The correct answer is __**Emerges undeviated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a ray of light passes through the **optical centre** of a spherical lens, it emerges **undeviated**, meaning it continues in the same direction without bending.
 
• The optical centre is the point inside the lens where the **principal axis** intersects, and it is the geometric center of the lens.
 
• This behavior occurs because, at the optical center, the two surfaces of the lens are **parallel** to each other, leading to no refraction or bending of light.
 
• The concept is governed by the laws of refraction, particularly Snell's Law, which ensures that light passing perpendicularly through parallel surfaces does not change its direction.
 
• This principle is applicable to both **convex** and **concave lenses**, irrespective of their thickness, provided the ray passes exactly through the optical center.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Spherical Lenses:**

 
 
• Spherical lenses are of two types: **convex** (converging lens) and **concave** (diverging lens).
 
• Convex lenses are thicker at the center and thinner at the edges, while concave lenses are thinner at the center and thicker at the edges.
 
 
 
• **Optical Centre:**
 
 
• The optical center is the central point of the lens where the principal axis passes through.
 
• It is the point where light rays pass without refraction if they enter the lens at this point.
 
 
 
• **Law of Refraction:**
 
 
• The refraction of light follows **Snell's Law**, which states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
 
• Light passing through parallel surfaces (like at the optical center) does not deviate because the angles of incidence and refraction cancel out.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Spherical Lenses:**
 
 
• Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses, cameras, and spectacles for correcting hypermetropia (farsightedness).
 
• Concave lenses are used in telescopes, microscopes, and spectacles for correcting myopia (nearsightedness).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Deviated Rays:** Light rays passing through regions other than the optical center of the lens are refracted and either converge (in convex lenses) or diverge (in concave lenses).
 
• **Principal Axis:** The principal axis is an imaginary straight line that passes through the center of curvature of both spherical surfaces of the lens.
 
• **Focal Point:** For convex lenses, light rays converge at the focal point, while for concave lenses, they appear to diverge from the focal point.
